content: A Diploma in Nursing, also referred to as a Nursing Diploma, is an entry-level tertiary education credential in the field of nursing. In the United States, this type of qualification is typically conferred by hospital-based nursing schools. Historically, all nurses in the United States were trained through diploma programs. During World War II, the Cherry Ames series of children's books was created to inspire young girls to pursue careers in nursing. The protagonist, Cherry Ames, was depicted as a nurse who had completed a hospital-based diploma program. Although the prevalence of hospital-based nursing schools has significantly declined over time, a number of these programs still operate. Some of these schools require applicants to complete non-nursing prerequisite courses at a separate institution prior to admission. Others coordinate their nursing curriculum with courses offered at nearby schools. However, many hospital-based nursing programs remain self-contained, offering all necessary coursework and clinical training within their own facilities.
